title: William Harvey (1578–1657) — Padua's Anatomy Theater, Venous Valves, the 1628 Stroke-Volume Proof, and Civil-War Exile

teenKit.tldr: For 1,400 years, doctors believed blood flowed out from the liver and burned up like fuel, until a short, dagger-wearing English physician named William Harvey proved it actually moves in one continuous closed loop.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how your heart pumps blood in a closed circle is the foundation of modern emergency medicine, surgery, and how we treat every single cardiovascular disease today.
keyTakeaways: In 1601 Padua, brilliant anatomy professor Hieronymus Fabricius looked right at venous valves—which only let blood flow toward the heart—yet completely misinterpreted them as gravity brakes due to ancient medical dogma.
William Harvey used strict mathematical proof in his 1628 book *De Motu Cordis* to show that the heart pumps more blood in an hour than the entire body could possibly manufacture from food.

Harvey's revolutionary theory lacked a microscopic link to prove how arteries connected to veins, a missing piece finally solved four years after his death when Marcello Malpighi used a lens to view capillaries in a frog's lung.

vocab.meaning: The surgical operation on a living animal for scientific experimentation to observe internal biological functions.
Tiny, pocket-like tissue flaps inside veins that act as one-way doors, forcing blood to travel toward the heart while preventing it from flowing backward.
The exact amount of blood pumped out of the heart's left ventricle with each individual heartbeat.
Microscopic, ultra-thin blood vessels that form the vital bridge connecting your arteries to your veins.

quiz.question: Why did professor Hieronymus Fabricius incorrectly conclude that venous valves were merely 'gravity breaks'?
options: He lacked the magnifying lens to see them clearly.
He was strictly blinded by an ancient 1,400-year-old medical dogma that blood flowed outward from the liver.
He only tested dead frogs instead of human cadavers.
He was forced by the church to hide his real findings.
quiz.explanation: Fabricius was trapped by the ancient belief system of Galen, making him misinterpret physical evidence that was right in front of his eyes.

quiz.question: What was the core breakthrough of William Harvey's 1628 mathematical proof in 'De Motu Cordis'?
options: He calculated that the heart pumps more blood daily than the liver could possibly produce or consume.
He discovered the exact microscopic structure of human lung tissue.
He proved that the brain controls the rhythm of the heartbeat.
He showed that blood is made entirely of water and salt.
quiz.explanation: Harvey used pure math to show the sheer volume of blood moving through the heart made the old liver-consumption theory totally impossible.

quiz.question: What crucial piece of the puzzle did Marcello Malpighi discover in 1661 using a microscope?
options: The molecular structure of oxygenated hemoglobin.
The electrical impulses that trigger a heartbeat.
The microscopic capillaries connecting arteries to veins.
The exact genetic code for heart muscle cells.
quiz.explanation: Malpighi found the invisible microscopic capillaries that proved how blood successfully completes its closed-loop journey.
